title: Prevent critical-result confirmation from impossible observation dates
prompt:
Fix timestamp acceptance in lib/ohworks-critical-repeat.ts. Lines 305-310 and 348-353 rely on Date.parse finiteness, allowing nonexistent dates to become apparently valid observations. I reproduced confirmed/repeat-not-required with reportValue=10 for a first result capturedAt=2026-02-30T12:00:00Z, matching synthetic subject/analyte and mmol/L units, repeatRequired=false, tolerance absolute=0.5/percent=10, maxRepeats=2, and no repeats. Confirmation bypasses the intended invalid-timestamp outcome. lib/ohworks-demo-critical-results-view.ts:51 consumes this evaluator for displayed critical-result evidence.

Validate actual calendar and clock fields for both first and repeat timestamps before chronological comparisons or confirmation. Keep valid Z and explicit-offset ISO timestamps accepted. For impossible first dates return discordant/first-result-timestamp-invalid; for impossible repeat dates return discordant/repeat-timestamp-invalid. Preserve null report values, notification behavior, repeat counts, matching rules, and numeric tolerance policy. Keep the helper local to this file.

Add tests/ohworks/critical-repeat-calendar.test.ts covering the no-repeat reproduction, an otherwise agreeing repeat with an impossible date, non-leap February 29, valid leap-day and offset controls. Assert exact status, reason, reportValue, and repeatsEvaluated. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks/critical-repeat.test.ts tests/ohworks/critical-repeat-calendar.test.ts tests/ohworks/demo-critical-results-view.test.ts.

Planning verification reproduced the defect and passed existing evaluator and demo-view tests. Modify only the named source and new test. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, auth, package.json, or workflow changes. work on the assigned branch you are on.
